name: Vow of Absolution

hooks.title: Ammunition Stores
hooks.text:
Scans of the Space Hulk, Persephone’s Regret, have been mostly inconclusive or interrupted by massive bouts of auspex interference. However recent successful deep scanning initiated by the Vow of Absolution has detected what appears to be a cache of Imperial ammunition and weaponry.

While the auspex readings may be inconclusive and any attempts at retrieval highly dangerous, the prospect of replenishment is too great an opportunity to bypass. Captain Akahir has made no secret of his disdain for the presence of Persephone’s Regret within the system or the danger it poses, and any additional damage the agents can inflict on the ominous ruin would be most welcomed by the Astartes.

gm:
The Vow of Absolution is a purpose-fitted battle barge. It was rearmed and resanctified to continue in the Imperium’s service when the Absolvers Chapter completed its founding in M34. The Adeptus Mechanicus reworked the vessel in its Jupiter shipyards for assignment to the newly designated Chapter. As the Chapter’s character and traditions began to coalesce, Chapter Master Dalir had the opportunity to give input on the vessel’s interior facilities and design. This allowed the incorporation of training and habitation choices more consistent with the emerging combat philosphies of the Chapter alongside the Chapter’s iconography. In this way, the vessel’s design reflected the Chapter Master’s vision for the Absolvers.

The Gilead Crusade served as the inaugural service for the vessel. The Vow made its first trip through the Warp as the crusade began. Even before reaching the Gilead System, Absolvers visited death worlds to recruit additional aspirants. During the early stages, the battle barge saw its first conflicts, and its Thunderhawks made their first landings on active targets. The Chapter’s morale was high, as their first few missions were early successes. The ship encountered only minor issues during this period, with a few quirks in life support and weapons systems that could be quickly repaired through the invocations and sanctified rituals of the Adeptus Mechanicus present. As the crusade proceeded, the vessel served honourably and with distinction. While it could not be present for every mission that included the Absolvers, it served bravely in the forefront of many of the Chapter’s earliest and most famous victories. The Chapter quickly took the Vow into their hearts and came to view the vessel as their home.

As the Crusade progressed, the Vow and the Chapter’s other voidcraft continued to serve in the Gilead System and the worlds beyond it. During this time, companies rotated between the different ships to give all of the Astartes opportunities to become familiar with each vessel. This also allowed the fledgling Astartes to truly get to know the machine spirits of each of their newly commissioned vessels.

After the liberation of the Gilead System, the Vow departed to continue with the Crusade. However, many Absolvers and several of the Chapter’s strike cruisers remained in the system to put down roots and begin the construction of planetside Chapter assets. During the later crusade, the Vow was involved in a fleet engagement with heretic forces and came under heavy fire from multiple battleships. The Absolvers ultimately played a crucial role in attaining victory, but the battle barge sustained crippling damage across several major systems. The damage set off a catastrophic chain of explosions that compromised significant armaments, defensive capabilities, and life support elements. The Vow was forced to limp back to the Gilead System for refit and repairs, while several strike cruisers were dispatched to take up the Absolvers’ mantle for the remainder of the Crusade.

By this time, the Absolvers’ Vow to defend the Gilead System was already in place, and Chapter Master Dalir insisted that the Chapter maintain a presence in the void. Rather than sending the Vow out of the Gilead System for a full refit, it remained in the system where Mechanicus adepts worked with Absolvers Techmarines to complete the necessary repairs. With the system’s limited repair facilities and scant resources, certainly compared to the great Jovian shipyards of the Adeptus Mechanicus, rumours abound that the Vow was never quite returned to full battle readiness. The Vow of Absolution has not left the Gilead System for many generations. The Chapter’s Vow is a key factor in this, but it may not be the only one. Some speculate that her engines are no longer fully functional. Some say that since the advent of the Noctis Aeterna, the ship’s Navigators have been unable to find safe passage out of the system for such a large vessel. However, the vessel does maintain its armoury of landing craft and boarding torpedoes. In recent years, these have seen service when Absolvers have acted to alleviate matters within Gilead directly.

… continues, VoA p.96

name: The Crucible of Command
gm:
The Absolvers consider the Vow’s command deck the intelligence and operations centre for all Imperial military action within the Gilead System. A massive holo-tank tracks supply chain activity, troop deployments, and all known active conflicts within the system. Scribes and servitors constantly work with a massive array of cogitators to update the tank’s information feed as new data come in from agents operating in the field. While these are not updated in real time, the system operates remarkably close to that level. This includes data from planetary communications networks and loyalist assets on the system’s various worlds and outposts. Reports from Absolvers units in the field are added to the feed as they are received, but with the reduced number of Space Marines in the system, this resource is more limited than usual. The battle barge’s sensors also contribute to the map, tracking the movements of other voidcraft. The holo-tank represents the most comprehensive and accurate military information available to the Imperium within the Gilead System. The Absolvers share this information with outsiders only when necessary.

Serfs, servitors, scribes, and Astartes constantly flow through the command deck, performing a poorly choreographed, ever-shifting dance as they update the holo-tank. Auto scribes and communications equipment chatter in the background while other sensors hum, buzz, and chirp with updated information. While the deck area is enormous, many areas become crowded when information flows from multiple sources simultaneously. This happens particularly often at those times when multiple Absolvers Kill Teams engage different enemies.

Brevet Captain Akahir is commonly found stalking the command deck. He spends much of his time in the holo-tank, scouring the various updates. During his study, he often directs questions to support staff regarding the information. In truth, most adepts who update the system are much more familiar with its intricacies than the Brevet Captain. His training with this device has been a baptism by fire, where he has been forced to learn how to use the system while using it. His lack of training further complicates this as he transitioned from Squad Sergeant to the position of Brevet Captain.

Akahir is not accustomed to commanding so many units or covering multiple operational theatres at once. While he has the inbuilt strategic brain of an Astartes, it takes time for a leader to move from commanding a squad of his brothers in a single battle to commanding hundreds of Space Marines across many different worlds. There have been issues with dispatching reinforcements to the wrong locations due to these complexities, but fortunately, these incidents have not been catastrophic.

name: Relics of War

hooks.title: Lost Relics
hooks.text:
Since the isolation of the Gilead System the Absolvers have implemented a number of protocols with the specific aim of conserving their limited resources. One such initiative commenced by Brevit Captain Akahir has been the increased deployment of the Chapters more esoteric arms from the reliquary onboard the Vow of Absolution.

However, Captain Akahir’s latest deployment has yet to return. The loss of a Chapter relic would a personal stain on Captain Akahir’s honor, worse still is the prospect of a powerful weapon falling into the hands of one of the many enemies of the Chapter that lurk in Gileads shadows.

gm:
The Absolvers do not have a single fortress monastery. Instead, they divide the functions it might perform across several places, including their battle barge. The Vow of Absolution's many responsibilities include serving as the Chapter’s main reliquary. This hallowed repository includes trophies of ancient conflicts, artefacts of past Chapter members, and much of the Chapter’s rarest pieces of wargear. At the coming of the Noctis Aeterana, when Chapter Master Erinyes dispersed the Chapter, he decreed that the Chapter’s vaults be opened so that worthy Absolvers might once more bear the Chapter’s ancient relics into battle. Many company commanders and veteran units swore vows as they took artefacts from the reliquary, including much of the Chapter’s Terminator and Artificer armour. Many of the Chapter’s Dreadnoughts also departed, though a few still slumber aboard the Vow, awaiting the call to battle.

Of the Absolvers within Gilead, only Chaplain Heractis is familiar with most relics remaining within the reliquary. The Chapter’s Techmarines can service most of these items but are unfamiliar with their history. Brevet Captain Akahir has had little opportunity to study these relics. Consequently, he has chosen to assign theseto chosen Astartes to complete missions at his behest and report their findings. In a few cases, he has also permitted Chaplain Heractis to assign artefacts to missions he directs from the Vault of Absolution.

ABSOLVERS CHAPTER BANNER

The Absolvers first used their Banner during their initial recruitment efforts during their journey to join the first wave of the Gilead Crusade. It first saw combat when the Absolvers deployed to seize Ostia as a beachhead in the system. Resistance was strong on that planet, and the Banner served as a critical rallying point for the battle-brothers of the young Chapter. Over the millennia, it has garnered many trophies and scars.

Absolvers who can see the Chapter Banner gain +2 bonus dice to any Leadership Test.

CHALICE OF ABSOLUTION

Upon his death in battle, an Absolvers Chaplain collected the blood of Chapter Master Emas Aneos. Legend has it that he transferred some of the blood to a chalice. In the days that followed, he offered a taste of it to each of the ten company Captains. After each had partaken, the Chaplain claimed to know which should succeed Aneos as the next Chapter Master. In the millennia since, the blood within the chalice has remained liquid, though it no longer serves as part of the Chapter Master selection process.

Any Absolvers acting in compliance with a Vow receives +2 bonus dice to all tests when in the presence of the Chalice of Absolution.

name: Castle Grigori

hooks.title: Raiders of the Wastes
hooks.text:
The Absolvers have made efforts to increase recruitment and bolster their forces within the Gilead System, encouraging greater numbers to undertake the arduous journey to Castle Grigori. Isolated and far from any semblance of Imperial protection, those that journey the wastelands are easy pickings for the nomadic recidivists and outlaws that lurk there.

Having neither the resources nor the will to commit to the continued protection of the routes that lead to Castle Grigori, those responsible have quickly resolved to root out the danger to their recruitment in its entirety and guarantee relative safety to those making their way to Castle Grigori.

hooks.title: Restless Slumber
hooks.text:
In the cavernous halls far beneath the active training fields and clamour of duelling cages sleep the ancient and most venerated of the Absolvers' warriors. Techmarines and their servitor assistants dwell in the soft glow of machine light as they attend to the slumber of these great war machines.

The regular dousing in sanctified oils, long and verbose prayers to the Machine God, and millennia worth of tradition ensure that the warriors within rest peacefully between deployments far from thoughts on the horror of their continued existence.

Yet the usually serene halls have, as of late, been interrupted. The Dreadnought that bears the name Bortu has unexpectedly woken several times, each time the result of its internal systems detecting the presence of an active homing beacon.

Most interestingly, the beacon itself is broadcasting from Gilead Primus, and while the ongoing isolation and turmoil of the Gilead System have brought some unrest to the planet, there are currently no major active deployments which would account for the beacon's presence.

Bortu is an ancient Dreadnought, entombed within his sarcophagus since the time of the Gilead Crusade, and the passing centuries have done nothing to calm his bellicose nature. As such, those within Castle Grigori have deemed it necessary to dispatch Agents to further investigate the signal in their efforts to soothe Bortu’s growing anger.

gm:
During the Gilead Crusade, the Absolvers made their initial landfall on the south pole of Gilead Primus. Even then, this region was little more than great swathes of uninhabited radioactive wastelands. These great irradiated plains were scarcely defended and the Absolvers were able to establish an effective beachhead at this site, construct temporary fortifications, and shuttle down supplies. The facility soon became a logistical centre as the invasion began to secure the planet. As the war continued, the Absolvers fortified this beachhead, gradually building it into a defensive complex which served more than just logistical purposes. By the time the planet had been brought fully into the fold of the Imperium, the roots of Castle Grigori ran so deep that it was deemed suitable for permanent occupation. Millennia later, it stands as a bastion of Imperial power and the seat of the Chapter's might within the Gilead System.

As at the time of its construction, Castle Grigori remains far from any of the planet’s hives or other Human enclaves. The planet’s southern polar region is a massive radioactive waste, yet the structure — and the untold thousands of its inhabitants within its sealed fortifications — are unaffected by that contamination. This provides further isolation that enables the resident Astartes and the many aspirants to perform their duties with little interruption.

The castle’s walls are armoured with thick layers of white ceramite. The colour choice, as well as the battering polar snow and ice, help to blend the enormous complex into the surrounding mountains. No roads lead to Castle Grigori. It sits at the centre of a semi-autonomous defensive network, monitored by hundreds of servitors and autocogitators. These systems are set to autotarget and destroy any vehicles that approach across the surface or sky, save for Absolvers Thunderhawks carrying supplies or relief units. Many of the massive weapons in the defence network were originally installed to defend the complex during the Gilead Crusade from attempts to repulse the Imperial invasion. Once the massive artillery emplacements were built, the Chapter decided it was wiser to leave them in place than to move them. Fortunately, the larger cannons have not had cause to fire in battle in centuries.

No one visits Castle Grigori lightly, and few visit it at all. Reaching the facility requires an isolated trek across hundreds of kilometres of radioactive polar wasteland. The massive complex and the Absolvers feature prominently in legends that circulate among Gilead Prime’s Human inhabitants. Because of these legends, many people talk about traveling to the castle to petition the Adeptus Astartes for aid, particularly when situations become particularly dire in their communities.

… continues, VoA p.100

name: Hall of Vows

hooks.title: Unfinished Vows
hooks.text:
Vows left unfinished by a fellow Absolver's death are treated with a sacred reverence, shaming both the memory of the fallen and the Chapter. The completion of these unfinished or failed vows is seen as a solemn undertaking by the ranks of the Absolvers, yet a necessary one.

As their continued defence of the beleaguered Gilead Syatem wears on, the pages of the Absolvers' records have become denser with ink than many consider acceptable. Master Loastin in particular is keen to see these unfinished deeds resolved and has recently begun to assign these broken vows to Scouts as one of the final parts of their training.

hooks.title: The Honoured Dead
hooks.text:
It is not unusual for Absolvers who fall in combat to die with Vows unfufilled. Normally these relate to the vows sworn for that particular battle that are quickly avenged or to long-standing oaths that are continued in the centuries following a battle-brother's death.

More unusual examples arise when Space Marines of the Absolvers undertake more esoteric missions, a more regular occurrence following the Gilead Systems isolation. Should an Absolver fall in battle deployed alongside other Imperial agents, there are no fellow battle- brothers present to uphold his vows, recover his equipment, or even honour his sacrifice.

Master Loastin can not abide this growing stain on the Chapter's honour and has recently begun sending Scouts and recently ascended Space Marines to retrieve their fallen brethren. Dispatched to some of the most deadly and dangerous battlefields across Gilead, these retrieval missions are a great honour to those undertaking them, despite the dangers faced.

gm:
Castle Grigori includes two distinct great halls. The Hall of Petitions is the more open of these spaces, allowing the coming and going of serfs and visiting dignitaries, but only full members of the Chapter, and those about to complete their initiation, are permitted to enter the Hall of Vows. The door is tightly secured with a lock that is gene-coded to only open to an individual who has been implanted with Absolvers gene-seed.

A member of the First Company always stands watch within the Hall. In fact, the guardians of the Hall of Vows are the only members of the Absolvers First Company who remain within the Gilead System. This sacred room is where initiates undertake their formal, ritualised admission to the Absolvers Chapter.

This massive chamber is large enough to accommodate three full companies of Space Marines. Despite this, the only light comes from spotlights focused to illuminate some of the Chapter’s past relics. These include tattered company banners, the most recently completed volume of The Book of Absolution, and other trophies. These relics hang from the walls or adorn marble columns and sculpted plinths. Notably, none of the relics remain as functional wargear. Everything displayed in this Hall holds historical value for the Absolvers, but has no battlefield role. Wargear that still functions is too precious to serve as museum pieces; each useful tool must remain where it is immediately accessible.

None of the usual devotional anthems play within the Hall. Instead, it is a place of resolute silence, save for the footfalls and recitations of Vows from the few who dare to tread through its vast emptiness. While any Absolvers may visit the chamber, few do so regularly, it is rare for more than a handful to enter the Hall of Vows at once. Instead, the oppressive silence and isolation serve as a reminder of the room’s sanctity. This also helps to create an environment where Absolvers can meditate with few distractions.

The ceiling and walls are illuminated, highlighting the detailed iconography painted and sculpted by the Absolvers during their recovery from past missions or as part of their meditation between training. Adeptus Astartes stationed at the Castle often use the Hall as a place to perform low concentration actions as they meditate. This is necessary, ase none of the Chapter’s serfs are permitted to enter the chamber even for maintenance or cleaning purposes. Some Absolvers choose to ritualistically clean the room, while others prefer to repaint the walls or even repair damaged illuminators. The Chapter regulations about intruders entering the Hall have remained inviolate for millennia. While it may simply be a matter of the isolation, the dimness, and the silence, many of the Absolvers believe that the Hall of Vows offers a connection to the spirits of brothers who have died in the Chapter’s service. Some claim to hear messages from fallen battle-brothers while they meditate within the room. Others profess to seeing visions of lost comrades here. The Chapter’s Librarians have inspected the chamber in response to many requests over the centuries, but they have never found any evidence of psychic activity.

… continues, VoA p.102

name: The Training Fields
gm:
All Absolvers since the Gilead Crusade have undergone training at Castle Grigori. This bastion represents a core element of their shared culture. Accomplished veterans who trained decades apart still share anecdotes about their education on its training fields — often under the same drill sergeants. Common topics of discussion include particularly brutal weather conditions in the polar fields, how much higher the radioactivity levels were in centuries past than today, and anecdotes about hunting the mutant terrors that haunt the fields. Of course, all pale in comparison to the favoured topic of discussion, the strict living conditions and brutal training regimens that the Chaplains and Sergeants enforce upon the aspirants.

Absolvers take several years to complete the full progression from aspirant to battle-brother. While they do depart the Castle to undertake missions, this is only once their training is nearly complete. Until that point, they spend their time studying the Codex Astartes and completing the brutal training to prepare their bodies and minds for the Astartes implants.

Certainly not everyone who attempts to join the Chapter achieves their goal. Many who survive the perilous journey across the polar radioactive wastes wash out early in the process. Some spend their lives as Absolvers serfs, others find only an early grave. Historically, Absolvers Chaplains travelled throughout the Gilead System and far beyond its boundaries to find recruits for the Chapter. They search for suitable aspirants in the black underpits of hive cities, and in the festering jungles of death worlds. They take only the very fiercest and most vicious children, many of whom have, in their short lives, already seen an existence of harshness undreamt of on more civilised Imperial worlds.

These provide the most exemplary recruits for the Astartes, with by far the highest chance of survival in the trials. Of course, even in these cases, the Chaplains are highly selective. Candidates whom they did not feel were likely to survive initiation were routinely delivered to other Imperial institutions, that they might still serve the Emperor.

Since the advent of the Noctis Aeterna, the Chapter has far less assets that they can commit to recruitment. They have not been able to send any Chaplains beyond the system’s boundaries to find recruits, and there have only been a handful of missions to other worlds within Gilead to find potential candidates.

While all of them have been brought back to Castle Grigori, the vast majority of candidates have come from Gilead Prime itself. In an unprecedented move, several dozen recruits have been shuttled directly to Castle Grigori from the hives, rather than requiring them to survive the trek across the polar wastes. Some Absolvers grumble about lowering the standards required for Astartes, others recognise that the Chapter does not have the same luxury of choice it used to.

FIELD WORK

Much of the training regimen takes place on Gilead Prime’s surface beyond the Castle. This territory is unforgiving. The Castle sits in the midst of a mountain range, which is riddled with natural caverns and ancient mines. Polar winds gust through the valleys and swirl about the peaks, carrying intense snow and ice storms. Radiation levels are high throughout the region, partly from bombs detonated during the Gilead Crusade and partly from fissionable materials recovered from the mines.

Mutated megafauna still wander the wasteland, millennia after the planet was pacified. Most make their homes in the subterranean areas, but some routinely travel to the surface in search of prey or to mate. The most deadly include the massive hornbat, which sometimes rides the polar winds in search of prey, and flamepelt-beetles, which emerge from their caves in search of prey to scorch and devour.

During training expeditions, aspirants spend weeks camping several kilometres from Castle Grigori and drilling with their weapons. Many die to megafauna in training incidents. More exceptional aspirants, however, capture trophies from these mutant creatures. Those who do so demonstrate the skill and determination that the Absolvers hope to find in their recruits. Training sergeants commend the initiative of these trainees, praising them and rewarding them with access to better conditions and more functional wargear.

… continues, VoA p.104

name: Hall of Petitions

hooks.title: Suspect Petitions
hooks.text:
The majority of petitions that reach the Absolvers at Castle Grigori from the few Imperial citizens who survive the long and dangerous pilgrimage are broad in scope. Often reflecting the superstitions and fears of those who deliver them from across Gilead Primus.

Recently however, there have been a number of petitions too specific in their nature to go unquestioned. On investigation, it has been found that those tasked with delivering them had been instructed or coerced into doing so. This is, at best, an affront and abuse of a centuries-old tradition and the Absolvers of Castle Grigori would like the mater investigated further.

gm:
The second great hall within Castle Grigori is a public facility. Visitors may enter the Hall of Petitions to request direct assistance from the Absolvers Chapter. For one hour each day, an Absolvers Chaplain attends to the line of alms seekers and responds to as many requests as possible in that time frame. Of course, the Chapter cannot take direct action for all of those who seek aid, but they do try to help those where it is both possible and appropriate.

The Absolvers have a legendary status amongst the people of the Gilead System, and the Hall of Petitions features prominently in that. There are countless legends of the Emperor’s Space Marines descending to right some wrong among the hives in response to a desperate plea for help. Petitioners who have not received a response to crises through traditional channels — especially those who live in the hive’s lower levels — know these stories and often act on them. Because of this, thousands of citizens queue for weeks waiting for their petition to be heard.

As they wait, the Chapter does little to care for the petitioners beyond the minimum necessary to keep the hall sanitary. Each must bring their own rations and appropriate survival gear. The hall is heated beyond the outside ambient polar temperatures, but the facility is kept at the lower end of the range of acceptable temperatures for an Astartes physique. Consequently, mortal Humans still die from exposure and radiation poisoning if they are not appropriately garbed. The Absolvers do not have the capacity to offer medicae facilities to those who need it. Instead, servitors routinely patrol the queue to dispose of those who died waiting.

Because of its location, completing the journey to Castle Grigori is extraordinarily difficult. Many who have spent their lives within Gilead Prime’s hives have little notion of the dangers inherent in the radioactive polar wilderness. Most also have no idea of the challenges involved in a lengthy journey afoot, as they are accustomed to routinely using their hive’s internal transit systems. In fact, the concepts of seasons and weather are completely foreign to many. Those who fail to plan their journey with this information arrive during the winter season, when temperatures are even more severe, severely compromising their chances of reaching Castle Grigori. Were it not for the mutated, predatory megafauna of the region, millions of corpses might litter the different routes that petitioners follow.

ANSWERED PRAYERS

The Absolvers have a long history within the Gilead System. Over the millennia, they have earned the respect of other Imperial organisations countless times. Few would dare to question their commitment to the system, and none would question their ability to handle any threat that might arise. As a result, the Absolvers proactively engage threats throughout the system, without waiting to inform the slow wheels of Imperial bureaucracy. This includes making raids on portions of the hives, or even some of the orbital stations when they identify a critical threat. Provided, of course, that they have the Astartes necessary to complete such missions.

However, many of the Imperium’s citizens have a poor understanding of the scope of their problems. Some beseech the Absolvers for aid when the issue is a problem with a facility’s technological infrastructure. A Chaplain has no resources to rebuild the crumbling levels of a hive. Similarly, the Astartes cannot increase food production, alter Imperial tithe schedules, or change the appearance of a memorial statue by means of a drop pod assault. The Absolvers are warriors who solve problems with the application of military force. When petitions can be answered through this tool, Chaplains try to act upon them. When the issues are outside of this scope, they simply send the petitioners on their way—sometimes directing them toward a more appropriate channel for aid.

… continues, VoA p.105

name: The Vault of Absolution
gm:
A small cluster of asteroids share orbit with one of Gilead Primus’ many moons. The Absolvers maintain the Vault of Absolution on one of these asteroids. This fortification is the site of one of their greatest assets and their gravest shame, for it is here that the Chapter sends those aspirants who fell prey to their Sanguine Visions. At the heart of this fortification, the Watchful monitor the Accursed, recording their Visions and piecing together prophecies. The Chaplain of Visions — currently Chaplain Heractis — then decides how to act upon these, usually either by informing the Chapter Master, directly dispatching a Kill Team, or by recording the information for future action.

The asteroid is small enough that it has little natural gravity and no atmosphere. Most of the Vault’s facilities are within adamantium reinforced tunnels deep beneath its surface. All exterior structures are thoroughly camouflaged to be indistinguishable from the surface. These include retractable doors for the hangar and weapons and sensor arrays. In fact, voidcraft visiting the facility must quell their primary engines at a specified distance when within the approach of the facility and complete landings, relying only on manoeuvring thrusters and the skill of the pilot. All of these steps are intended to keep the facility secret from outsiders, including other Imperial organisations.

Though the Adeptus Mechanicus certainly played a critical role in building the Vault, it did so with the utmost discretion. While details remain lost to the ages, it is believed that the Adeptus Mechanicus were bound to all records of the facility. In the millennia since its construction, only full members of the Chapter and its most trusted serfs have been stationed here, the latter usually knowing that they will never leave. Few outsiders have even an inkling of the facility’s existence. Of those who have reason to believe that the Absolvers might maintain another bastion within the Gilead System, none know its true purpose. There are no official records of the Vault of Absolution anywhere outside of the Chapter. Absolvers pilots memorise the navigational coordinates of the Vault and navigate manually during each trip. None of these may be written down or annotated on any maps, lest they fall into the hands of an outsider.

In fact, most Absolvers remain unaware that those battle-brothers who fell prey to their Sanguine Visions are even kept alive. They believe that the failed aspirants died during the final stages of the Black Carapace surgery. Outside of Chapter Command, only Apothecaries, some Chaplains, and the Watchful are fully aware of the true tragedy. Many more are aware that the Chapter has access to prophecies discovered from the tragic Visions, but they do not realise that many of the Accursed seers remain alive, often expanding upon the scope of the prophecies.

The Vault maintains a strict policy of isolation and monitors any who intrude upon its space. Its defensive capabilities are well concealed but comparable to those of an Imperial battleship. Consequently, any smaller craft, even Imperial ones, that show any sign of inquisitive interest or begin an unauthorised approach are dealt with quickly and permanently. In addition, the base maintains several boarding torpedoes. In the eventuality that a vessel approaches that cannot be eliminated quickly by the station’s firepower, Watchful may use those torpedoes to commence boarding actions.

Castle Grigori handles the Vault’s logistics. This includes the transfer of supplies and personnel, as well as any new Accursed. Personnel and supply transfers are the only travel directly between the Castle and the Vault. Except in the most extreme emergencies, Kill Teams dispatched from the Vault travel to Castle Grigori as the first stop along their mission to maintain the Vault’s security and secrecy, while Watchful stationed in the Vault are recorded as being assigned to Castle Grigori. Any Space Marine units dispatched to other parts of the system can only be tracked back to either Castle Grigori or the Vow of Absolution as their point of origin.

THE ACCURSED AND THE WATCHFUL

Both physical manifestation of the Absolvers’ greatest shame, and potentially their greatest asset, these fallen brethren are the legacy of heretical tampering with Sanguinius’ blessed gene-seed. While those involved have since paid for this blasphemy, without those manipulations, the Chapter would never have had access to the prophecies that the Accursed reveal through their Sanguine Visions. Those divinations have enabled the Absolvers to save millions of lives, guiding them to the time and place where they can serve the Imperium the most. However, the Absolvers dare not share the existence of these prophecies with even the most trusted of outsiders.

… continues, VoA p.108

name: The Vault of the Endless Watch
gm:
While the Vault of Absolution is located on an asteroid, it is functionally an isolated space station. There is no natural light and no exposure to the natural world. The only living beings beyond the Absolvers are a few pets and small plants that some of the Accursed tend to under the supervision of the Watchful.

The Watchful can travel freely about the facility. This includes access to the hangars, the armoury, their quarters, and a few other basic facilities to enable them to continue their lives as Adeptus Astartes. None of these are luxurious, but they provide some respite from the task of caring for their fallen brethren.

The Watchful call the core of the facility the Vault of the Endless Watch. This is the section where the Accursed are kept safe, so that the Watchful can decipher their Sanguine Visions. These cells are roughly square, with sides about two metres wide, and ceilings 3 metres tall for easy movement of Astartes. The doors are forged of thick ceramite, with hinges and locks capable of resisting even the superhuman strength of an Adeptus Astartes. The chambers are densely arranged together, to make maximum use of the available space, and to also enable Watchful to quickly move between cells in case of any incidents. The downside for the Accursed is that smells and sounds carry between the various cells.

Accursed have access to only the starkest accommodations. Most are imprisoned and physically bound to their billets to prevent them from doing further damage to themselves — and their gene-seed — as they struggle with their Sanguine Visions. At the discretion of a Watchful, some may have their bonds released so that they can exercise, study, pray, practice basic self-care, or even engage in basic forms of artistic endeavour. However even these freedoms only happen within their small cells. There have been too many incidents where Accursed suddenly suffered an onset of the Red Thirst and attacked their brethren for the Absolvers to take further chances.

Medicae servitors constantly roam the halls and visit the rooms of the most incapacitated Accursed. They provide the basic care necessary to sustain these suffering individuals. They also maintain extensive records of each brother’s medical status, so that Apothecaries can easily keep abreast of any anomalies. While the health of every Adeptus Astartes is important, when an Accursed begins to decline, it typically indicates that they are getting closer to their moment of death. As this approaches, their Sanguine Visions are more likely to reach fruition. Chaplain Heractis must be kept informed of this progress, so that he can be prepared to take any necessary actions based upon that Vision.

RECORDING VISIONS

The majority of the Accursed are incapable of deliberately communicating with the world outside their Sanguine Visions. Because of this, it is very hard for most Watchful to record their Visions and assemble them into a useful divination. In some cases, the Accursed may be able to verbalise their experiences, as if speaking from a dream. While these are mostly screams of anger or agony, some jumbled phrases can make it through. Those Watchers who record these outbursts can come away with new and disturbing insights into the suffering of the Accursed.

Fortunately, Absolvers Librarians have more direct tools available to understand the Accursed’s Visions. They can read their minds and draw upon the memories of the Visions, sometimes even experiencing them as the Accursed suffer through them. These efforts are not without risk. Many Librarians have become trapped within these Visions. Those who escape from the Visions record what they have seen, and use the information to create a more accurate prophecy. In rare cases where a Librarian does not emerge from this state, they are added to the ranks of the Accursed.

Because each Accursed’s Sanguine Visions encompass days or even weeks, fully deciphering one may take many telepathic sessions. Finding the correct memories amidst the many iterations of the Visions can be particularly challenging. With each trip into a corrupted mind, the Librarian incurs ever greater risk of being trapped within the experience.
